text: What distinguishes 'embedded' cognition from 'extended' cognition within the 4E framework?
choices: Embedded cognition claims the mind reaches into the environment, while extended cognition denies any environmental role
Embedded and extended cognition are simply two names for the same Clark-Chalmers thesis

Embedded cognition holds that cognitive processes depend heavily on environmental scaffolding but still occur in the brain, whereas extended cognition holds they literally include environmental elements as constituents
Embedded cognition is a form of substance dualism, while extended cognition is physicalist
explanation: The embedded view is the more conservative one: the brain does the cognizing but leans essentially on external scaffolding (notebooks, calendars); the extended view is the radical constitutive claim that the external resource is literally part of the cognitive process. Option 0 reverses the two; option 1 conflates them; option 3 misdescribes both, which are naturalistic.
